process_area.title: Drug-Free Workplace Policy, Framework & DOLE Compliance

fields.Participants: HR (VS-103), HSE (VS-24), Compliance (VS-22), Legal (VS-100), Occupational Health (VS-83), Labor Relations (VS-84), Security (VS-23)
fields.Volume: One enterprise drug-free workplace program across 5 entities

workflows.name: Drug-Free Workplace Strategy, Policy & Operating Model

Automation Opportunity: - Policy library; acknowledgement-tracking; onboarding/handbook integration; change-cascade
Controls: - CTL-680: written DOLE-aligned policy; scope all entities/roles; rehabilitation pathway; acknowledged by all employees; reviewed annually
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-100 (legal), VS-24 (HSE), VS-84 (labor/CBA), VS-19 (onboarding), W4458 (regulatory), W4473 (rehab)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Policy-absence risk**: no written policy → DOLE D.O. 53-03 non-compliance + officers' RA 9165 liability; mitigated by documented policy
- **Punitive-only risk**: pure-punishment program conflicts with DOLE rehabilitation emphasis + morale; mitigated by rehabilitation pathway (W4473)
System Touchpoints: - HRIS/policy (VS-19/VS-103); compliance (VS-22); legal (VS-100); HSE (VS-24); labor (VS-84); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: HR/HSE/Compliance set the drug-free strategy & policy — objectives (safety, legal compliance, deterrence, rehabilitation), scope (all entities/sites/roles incl. safety-sensitive), and the prevention-vs-punishment balance (DOLE rehabilitation emphasis)

HR/Legal draft the written policy (required by D.O. 53-03) — prohibited conduct, testing types & circumstances, consequences, rehabilitation pathway, confidentiality, due process — and align with the CBA/handbook (VS-84)
HR/Compliance cascade the policy to all employees (acknowledgement), embed in onboarding/handbook (VS-19), and review on regulatory/incident change

fields.Participants: Compliance (VS-22), HR (VS-103), Legal (VS-100), HSE (VS-24), Occupational Health (VS-83), DOLE/Liaison (VS-104)

workflows.name: DOLE D.O. 53-03 & PH Regulatory Framework Alignment

Automation Opportunity: - Regulatory-change monitoring; compliance-calendar auto-populate; inspection-readiness checklist; accreditation verification
Controls: - CTL-680: regulatory framework mapped; policy/program aligned; labs/MRO DOH-accredited; DOLE documentation ready (W4477)
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-100 (legal), VS-104 (govt affairs), VS-36 (governance), W4457 (policy), W4460 (vendor), W4477 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Regulatory-blindness risk**: missed D.O./RA 9165 update → non-compliance; mitigated by regulatory-change monitoring
- **Lab/MRO-accreditation risk**: using non-DOH-accredited lab → invalid results + penalty; mitigated by accreditation verification (W4460)
System Touchpoints: - Compliance (VS-22); legal (VS-100); HRIS (VS-19/VS-103); HSE (VS-24); DOLE liaison (VS-104); records (VS-88)

steps.activity: Compliance/Legal map the regulatory framework — DOLE D.O. 53-03 (drug-free workplace policy/program), RA 9165 Art. V (employer obligation & officer liability), DOH A.O. (accredited drug-testing labs/MRO), LTFRB/DOTr (driver testing), and DOLE D.O. on workplace safety
Compliance/HR translate regulations into the policy (W4457), the testing matrix (W4465–W4468), vendor accreditation (W4460), and DOLE documentation (W4477)
Compliance/Legal monitor regulatory change, manage DOLE inspection (W4477), and report to governance (VS-36/W4480)

fields.Participants: HR (VS-103), HSE (VS-24), Fleet (VS-06), Store Ops (VS-07), Occupational Health (VS-83), Contingent (VS-98)
fields.Volume: Safety-sensitive population (operators, drivers, chemical handlers) across 5 entities

Automation Opportunity: - Role-classification engine; safety-sensitive flag in HRIS; license/certification tracking; auto-inclusion of contingent
Controls: - CTL-680: safety-sensitive roles classified & flagged; testing-frequency per class; driver license/cert tracked; contingent included (W4463)
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (fleet/driver), VS-24 (HSE), VS-98 (contingent), VS-147 (customer safety), W4457 (policy), W4466–W4468 (testing)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-classification risk**: safety-sensitive role not flagged → under-tested → impairment risk; mitigated by structured classification & review
- **Driver-license-gap risk**: driver without valid LTFRB license/cert → regulatory + safety risk; mitigated by license tracking (VS-06)
System Touchpoints: - HRIS/job/role (VS-19/VS-103); HSE (VS-24); fleet/driver (VS-06.2); license (VS-06); contingent (VS-98); customer safety (VS-147)

steps.activity: HR/HSE/Fleet identify & classify **safety-sensitive** roles — powered-equipment operators (forklift/reach/order-picker), delivery drivers (LTFRB/DOTr-regulated), paint/chemical/hazmat handlers, equipment operators, security with firearm, and any role where impairment risks severe harm (links VS-147)

HR/HSE set the testing-frequency/intensity per role class — safety-sensitive: random + post-incident + reasonable-suspicion + return-to-duty; non-safety-sensitive: pre-employment + reasonable-suspicion — per policy (W4457)
HR/Fleet/Contingent flag safety-sensitive employees in HRIS, ensure license/certification (LTFRB for drivers), and extend requirements to contingent/contractor (W4463)

fields.Participants: Procurement (VS-34), Occupational Health (VS-83), HR (VS-103), Legal (VS-100), Compliance (VS-22), Privacy (VS-91), Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Volume: Collection-site / DOH-accredited lab / MRO vendor relationship

Automation Opportunity: - Accreditation verification & monitoring; SLA dashboard; chain-of-custody tracking; vendor performance scorecard
Controls: - CTL-680: vendor DOH-accredited (lab/MRO); chain-of-custody contracted; RA 10173 data-protection; SLA-governed; accreditation maintained
Cross-references: - links to VS-34 (procurement), VS-83 (occupational health), VS-100 (legal), VS-91 (privacy), VS-22 (compliance), W4458 (regulatory), W4469 (collection)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Non-accredited-vendor risk**: invalid results + penalty; mitigated by DOH-accreditation verification & maintenance clause
- **Chain-of-custody-break risk**: specimen handling gap → challengeable result; mitigated by contractual chain-of-custody terms
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/contract (VS-34); occupational health (VS-83); legal (VS-100); privacy (VS-91); compliance (VS-22); finance (VS-17.4); records (VS-88)
Time Estimate: - ~3–4 weeks per contract cycle; ongoing governance

steps.activity: Procurement/Occupational Health select **DOH-accredited** drug-testing laboratory, collection sites/clinic, and a Medical Review Officer (MRO), verifying accreditation, methodology, chain-of-custody, turnaround, and data security
Legal/Privacy contract the vendor with SLA, **chain-of-custody** terms, confidentiality/RA 10173 data-protection, accreditation-maintenance, audit rights, and breach consequence
Occupational Health/HR govern vendor performance (turnaround, accuracy, accreditation, data security), review periodically, and enforce consequence on breach

fields.Participants: L&D (VS-19.4), HR (VS-103), HSE (VS-24), Compliance (VS-22), Supervisors/Managers, Occupational Health (VS-83)

Automation Opportunity: - e-learning + completion tracking; supervisor reasonable-suspicion module; awareness-survey analytics
Controls: - CTL-680 (ensure controlled execution — Drug-Free Workplace Policy, Framework & DOLE Compliance (PA-150.1).)
- CTL-680: curriculum covers policy/testing/rehab/EAP; onboarding+annual+supervisor; contingent included; supportive culture
Cross-references: - links to VS-19.4 (L&D), VS-103 (HR), VS-24 (HSE), VS-83.3 (EAP), VS-22 (compliance), W4457 (policy), W4467 (reasonable suspicion), W4473 (rehab)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Supervisor-untrained risk**: supervisors can't recognize reasonable-suspicion → missed intervention; mitigated by supervisor training
- **Punitive-culture risk**: fear-only culture → under-reporting/no rehabilitation uptake; mitigated by supportive/rehabilitation messaging
System Touchpoints: - L&D (VS-19.4); HRIS/competency (VS-103); HSE (VS-24); compliance (VS-22); EAP (VS-83.3); records (VS-88)
Time Estimate: - ~1 hr onboarding + ~1 hr annual + ~2–4 hr supervisor training per head

steps.activity: L&D/HR/HSE build the curriculum — policy (W4457), dangers of drugs, testing circumstances (W4465–W4468), consequences, rehabilitation pathway (W4473), supervisor reasonable-suspicion recognition, and EAP awareness
L&D deliver (onboarding + annual + supervisor reasonable-suspicion training), track completion, and target contingent workforce too (W4463)
HR/HSE build a supportive culture (rehabilitation-not-punitive-only), communicate deterrent effect, and measure awareness (W4478)

fields.Participants: Privacy/DPO (VS-91), HR (VS-103), Legal (VS-100), Occupational Health (VS-83), Compliance (VS-22), Vendor (VS-34)

workflows.name: Drug Testing Consent, Privacy (RA 10173) & Confidentiality Framework

Automation Opportunity: - Consent-capture workflow; restricted-access results vault; retention automation; DSAR workflow; access-audit
Controls: - CTL-680 (ensure controlled execution — Drug-Free Workplace Policy, Framework & DOLE Compliance (PA-150.1).)
- CTL-680: informed consent per test; need-to-know access; secure storage/transfer; retained per policy; labor-lawful use (due process); privacy-audited
Cross-references: - links to VS-91 (privacy), VS-83 (occupational health), VS-100 (legal), VS-88 (records), VS-84 (labor), VS-91.3 (breach), W4471 (due process), W4476 (confidentiality)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Privacy-breach risk**: drug-test result disclosed → RA 10173/NPC exposure + employee claim; mitigated by need-to-know access & secure storage
- **Consent-gap risk**: testing without informed consent → challengeable/labor-risk; mitigated by per-test consent protocol
System Touchpoints: - Privacy/DPO (VS-91); occupational health (VS-83); legal (VS-100); records (VS-88); compliance (VS-22); labor (VS-84); breach (VS-91.3)

steps.activity: DPO/Legal/Occupational Health set the consent & lawful-basis framework — informed consent per test, sensitive-data (health) handling under RA 10173, purpose limitation (employment/health/safety), and access restriction
HR/Occupational Health/Vendor handle results confidentially — restricted access (need-to-know), secure storage/transfer, retention (VS-88), and DSAR handling (VS-91)
DPO/Compliance audit privacy compliance, manage any breach (VS-91.3), and ensure labor-lawfulness of results use (due process W4471, VS-84)

fields.Participants: Contingent Workforce (VS-98), HR (VS-103), Procurement (VS-34), HSE (VS-24), Legal (VS-100), Fleet (VS-06/VS-56)
fields.Volume: ~10–20% contingent labor (security, janitorial, promodizers, agency labor, delivery partners)

Automation Opportunity: - Agency-compliance verification gate; contractor induction/access control; on-site audit checklist; non-compliance workflow
Controls: - CTL-680 (ensure controlled execution — Drug-Free Workplace Policy, Framework & DOLE Compliance (PA-150.1).)
- CTL-680: contractor/agency drug-free coverage in contract; safety-sensitive verified/inducted; non-compliant excluded; adherence audited on-site
Cross-references: - links to VS-98 (contingent), VS-34 (procurement), VS-24 (HSE), VS-147/W4390 (customer/contractor safety), VS-06/VS-56 (fleet/partner), W4457 (policy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Contractor-gap risk**: agency worker not tested → impaired operator on BuildRight site → BuildRight premises liability (VS-147); mitigated by contractual coverage & verification
- **Enforcement-gap risk**: requirement in contract but not verified; mitigated by on-site audit & exclusion authority
System Touchpoints: - Contingent workforce (VS-98); procurement/contract (VS-34); HSE (VS-24); legal (VS-100); fleet/partner (VS-06/VS-56); security/access (VS-23)

steps.activity: Procurement/Contingent/Legal set the contractor/agency drug-free coverage requirement — agency obligation to test its workers (esp. safety-sensitive on BuildRight sites: agency forklift operators, security, promodizers), in the service contract
Contingent/HSE verify agency compliance (agency testing records/cert), induct safety-sensitive contractors (VS-147/W4390), and exclude non-compliant workers from BuildRight sites
HSE/Contingent audit contractor adherence on-site, remove impaired/non-compliant workers, and enforce contractual consequence

fields.Participants: HR (VS-103), IT (VS-27), EA (VS-113), Occupational Health (VS-83), Privacy (VS-91), Legal (VS-100), BI (VS-28)
fields.Trigger: Program setup; system lifecycle; data need

workflows.name: Drug-Free Program Data, Records & System Architecture

Automation Opportunity: - Integrated testing/case/EAP platform; restricted-access health-data vault; analytics dashboard; retention automation
Controls: - CTL-680 (ensure controlled execution — Drug-Free Workplace Policy, Framework & DOLE Compliance (PA-150.1).)
- CTL-680: architecture security-assessed (VS-27.3); health-data privacy-by-design (VS-91); SoD; records retained (VS-88); cost governed (VS-135)
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HRIS), VS-83 (occupational health), VS-27 (IT), VS-91 (privacy), VS-88 (records), W4462 (consent/privacy), W4478 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-silo risk**: testing data not linked to HRIS/occupational-health → program blind spots; mitigated by integration
- **Health-data-exposure risk**: sensitive results exposed; mitigated by privacy-by-design & restricted access
System Touchpoints: - HRIS (VS-103); occupational health (VS-83); IT (VS-27); EA (VS-113); privacy (VS-91); records (VS-88); legal (VS-100); BI (VS-28); TBM (VS-135)

steps.activity: HR/EA/IT design the data architecture — testing records (consent W4462, result, MRO, chain-of-custody), safety-sensitive flag (W4459), case management (W4471), EAP/referral (W4473), with restricted access & integration to HRIS (VS-103)/occupational-health (VS-83)
IT/Privacy implement with health-data sensitivity (RA 10173), secure evidence/records retention (VS-88), SoD, and integration to compliance (VS-22)/legal (VS-100)
HR/IT govern the platform, drive analytics (W4478), and optimize on adoption/cost (VS-135)
